[0-0-2.5] Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in the Integrated Sciences specialization.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Models in Science
description: Meaning, nature, use, strengths and limitations of models as investigative tools in all scientific disciplines. Detailed investigation of selected model systems from different scientific disciplines. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. [2-0-2] Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

name: Ethical Issues in Science
description: Theoretical and practical consideration of ethics in the practice, reporting, public impact and accountability of science. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third-year standing in any faculty.

name: Non-Animal Methods in Biomedical Science
description: Interdisciplinary non-animal methods (e.g., organoids, organ-on-a-chip, 3D bioprinting) for research, testing, and education; the regulatory landscape. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Directed Studies
description: Permission of the Director is required.

name: Interdisciplinary Honours Thesis
description: Original research work under the guidance of a faculty member. Registration by approval of the Integrated Sciences Director.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Comparative Field Research Course: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Systems science approaches encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems to investigate, analyze and research two unique regions of the world. Course location may vary; course location must be different than ISCI 361; fee payable prior to field course. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: ISCI 361.

name: Student Directed Seminars
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 399.

name: Co-Operative Work Placement IV
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 498.

name: Directed Studies
description: A research project approved by the supervisor in the field of interest of the student designed to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. Note: the supervisor may be teaching at the Marine Centre; or a member of faculty of WCUMSS whether at the Marine Centre as a research investigator or as one of the members of WCUMSS.

name: Special Topics in Marine Biology
description: This course will be offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. It is expected that the course will generally be of a specialized nature and be at a level appropriate to graduate or senior undergraduate students.

name: Special Topics in Marine Biology
description: This course will be offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. This course will be of a specialized nature and at a level appropriate to graduate or senior undergraduate students.

name: Marine Invertebrate Zoology
description: A survey of the marine phyla, with emphasis on the benthic fauna in the vicinity of the Marine Station. The course includes lectures, laboratory periods, field collection, identification and observation. Emphasis is placed on the study of living specimens in the laboratory and in the field.

name: Comparative Invertebrate Embryology
description: A comprehensive study of development of marine invertebrates available at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre, including all major phyla and most of the minor phyla. Prerequisite: course in invertebrates or embryology.

name: Biology of Fishes
description: Classification, physiology, ecology, behaviour and zoogeography of fishes with particular emphasis on those in the marine environment of the British Columbia coast. Prerequisite: A course in comparative vertebrate anatomy.

name: Structure and Function in Marine Animals
description: Principles of classification, evolution, morphology, biomechanics, physiology and biochemistry will be illustrated in representatives from a variety of animal phyla. [3-3-0] Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Marine Phycology
description: A survey of the marine algae, with emphasis on the benthic forms in the vicinity of the Marine Centre. The course includes lectures, laboratory periods, field collection, identification and observation. Emphasis is placed on the study of living specimens in the laboratory and in the field.

name: Ecological Adaptations of Seaweeds
description: Morphological, physiological, genetic and reproductive adaptations of seaweeds to their environments. [3-3-0] Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Marine Ecology
description: An analytical approach to biotic associations in the marine environment. Opportunities are provided for study of the intertidal realm in exposed and protected areas, and of beaches and estuaries in the vicinity of the Marine Centre; plankton studies and investigations of the subtidal and benthic environments by diving and dredging are envisaged.

name: Introduction to Biological Oceanography
description: An introduction to the biology of oceans, with supporting coverage of relevant physics and chemistry. Emphasis will be placed on plankton biology, community structure and life histories, and influencing environmental factors. Collections will be made from sheltered inlets, through Barkely Sound to offshore waters. The course will involve both field and laboratory. Prerequisite: All of BIOL_V 320, BIOL_V 205

name: Population and Community Ecology of Marine Organisms
description: Emphasis on interactions among organisms and between organisms and their physiochemical environment, and on biological diversity. [3-3-0] Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Biology of Marine Birds
description: Study of interrelationship of birds and the marine environment. Census techniques and observation of birds in the field will be emphasized. Prerequisite: Completion of a course in vertebrate zoology or permission of the instructor.

name: Biology of Marine Mammals
description: Survey course covering systematics and distribution of marine mammals, their sensory capabilities and physiology, with special emphasis on the Cetacea. The course will involve an independent field study. Prerequisite: Introductory vertebrate zoology.

name: Seminars and Papers in Marine Science
description: Instruction in the critical analysis of published research papers and of oral seminars. [2-2-0] Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Special Topics
description: 6 weeks. Offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists who are visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. The course will be of a specialized nature.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Special Topics
description: 3 weeks. Offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists who are visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. The course will be of a specialized nature.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Differential Calculus with Applications
description: Derivatives of elementary functions. Applications and modelling: graphing, optimization. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: A score of 80% or higher in BC Pre-calculus 12. High school calculus is strongly recommended.

name: Integral Calculus with Applications
description: The definite integral, integration techniques, applications, modelling, infinite series. Equivalency: MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100.

name: Differential Calculus with Applications to Life Sciences
description: Functions, derivatives, optimization, growth and decay, discrete probability. Equivalency: MATH_V 100, 104. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: High-school calculus and a score of 80% or higher in BC Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12.

name: Integral Calculus with Applications to Life Sciences
description: Antiderivatives and definite integrals, infinite series, applications to probability and dynamical systems. Equivalency: MATH_V 101, 105. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184.

name: Differential Calculus with Applications to Commerce and Social Sciences
description: Derivatives and rates of change, exponential and trigonometric functions, Newton's method, Taylor polynomials, maxima and minima, and graphing. Equivalency: MATH_V 100, 102. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: High-school calculus and a score of 80% or higher in BC Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12.

name: Integral Calculus with Applications to Commerce and Social Sciences
description: Antiderivatives, the definite integral, techniques of integration, infinite series, partial derivatives, maxima and minima with constraints, discrete and continuous random variables. Equivalency: MATH_V 101, 103. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

name: Differential Calculus
description: Topics as for MATH 100, but including relevant topics from algebra, geometry, functions, trigonometry, logarithms, and exponentials. [3-0-1.5; 3-0-1.5] Prerequisite: A grade of 65% or higher in BC Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12.

name: Matrix Algebra
description: Systems of linear equations, operations on matrices, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization of symmetric matrices. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Equivalency: MATH_V 221. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100 or (b) advanced credit for MATH_V 100, or (c) SCIE_V 001 as a co-requisite.

name: Honours Differential Calculus
description: Limits, derivatives, Mean Value Theorem and applications, elementary functions, optimization, Taylor series, approximation. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[4-0-0] Prerequisite: High-school calculus and one of (a) a score of 95% or higher in BC Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12; or (b) permission from the Mathematics Department Head.

name: Honours Integral Calculus
description: Definite integrals and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, techniques and applications of integration, infinite series. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [4-0-0] Prerequisite: Either a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH_V 120, b) a score of 80% or higher in MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, or c) a score of 5 in AP Calculus AB.

name: Honours Linear Algebra
description: Matrices, eigenvectors, diagonalization, orthogonality, linear systems, applications. Students who obtain credit for MATH_V 131 cannot in the same or later terms obtain credit for MATH_V 111, MATH_V 152, or MATH_V 221. [3-0-0] Equivalency: MATH_V 223. Prerequisite: One of (a) one of MATH_V 120, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, or (c) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 111, MATH_V 221, or (d) SCIE_V 001 as a corequisite.

name: Linear Systems
description: 2D and 3D geometry, vectors and matrices, eigenvalues and vibration, physical applications. Laboratories demonstrate computer solutions of large systems. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-1*-0] Corequisite: MATH_V 101.

name: Differential Calculus with Applications
description: Topics as for Math 100; intended for students with no previous knowledge of Calculus. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. Not for credit for students with AP Calculus AB, AP Calculus BC, or a passing score on the UBC-SFU-UVIC-UNBC Calculus Challenge Examination. [3-0-1.5] Prerequisite: A grade of 80% or higher in BC Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12.

name: Differential Calculus for Social Science and Commerce
description: Topics as for Math 104; intended for students with no previous knowledge of Calculus. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. Not for credit for students with AP Calculus AB, AP Calculus BC, or a passing score on the UBC-SFU-UVIC-UNBC Calculus Challenge Examination. [3-0-1.5] Prerequisite: A grade of 80% or higher in BC Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12.

name: Calculus Survey
description: Functions, derivatives, integrals, curve sketching growth functions, volume calculations. Only for credit in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Students with credit for MATH_V 100, 102, 104, 120, 180, or 184 cannot in the same term or later terms obtain credit for MATH_V 190. [3-0-2] Prerequisite: Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12 and registration in the B.S.F. or B.Sc.N. programs.

name: Calculus III
description: Analytic geometry in 2 and 3 dimensions, partial and directional derivatives, chain rule, maxima and minima, second derivative test, Lagrange multipliers, multiple integrals with applications. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103.

name: Introduction to Mathematical Computing
description: Introduction to mathematical software and numerical methods. Numbers, arrays, functions, vectorization and iteration. Sequences and series, root finding, numerical integration, numerical methods for differential equations, systems of linear equations, mathematical graphics. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 215, MATH_V 255, MATH_V 256, MATH_V 258, MATH_O 225 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

name: Elementary Differential Equations I
description: First-order equations; linear equations; linear systems; Laplace transforms; numerical methods; trajectory analysis of plane nonlinear systems. Applications of these topics will be emphasized. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200.

name: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
description: Partial differentiation, extreme values, multiple integration, vector fields, line and surface integrals, the divergence theorem, Green's and Stokes' theorems. Intended for students in Honours Physics and Engineering Physics. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[4-0-0] Prerequisite: A score of 68% or higher in one of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 158, SCIE_V 001 and a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

name: Mathematical Proof
description: Sets and functions; induction; cardinality; properties of the real numbers; sequences, series, and limits. Logic, structure, style, and clarity of proofs emphasized throughout. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 64% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 or (b) one of MATH_V 121, MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200.

name: Matrix Algebra
description: Systems of linear equations, operations on matrices, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization of symmetric matrices. This course is intended for first and second year students. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Equivalency: MATH_V 111. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 100 or (b) advanced credit for MATH_V 100, or (c) SCIE_V 001 as a corequisite.

name: Honours Linear Algebra
description: Matrices, eigenvectors, diagonalization, orthogonality, linear systems, applications. This course is intended for first and second year students. Students who obtain credit for MATH_V 223 cannot in the same or later terms obtain credit for MATH_V 111, MATH_V 152, or MATH_V 221. [3-0-0] Equivalency: MATH_V 131. Prerequisite: One of (a) one of MATH_V 120, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100, or (c) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 111, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103, MATH_O 221, or (d) SCIE_V 001 as a corequisite.

name: Advanced Calculus I
description: Functions of several variables: limits, continuity, differentiability; implicit functions; Taylor's theorem; extrema; Lagrange multipliers; multiple integration, Fubini's theorem; improper integrals. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH_V 121 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

name: Advanced Calculus II
description: Parametrization of curves and surfaces; line and surface integrals; theorems of Green, Gauss, Stokes; applications to physics and/or introduction to differential forms. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 226. Prerequisite grade requirement: 68% in MATH226.

name: Marvels of Mathematics
description: A variety of topics in mathematics, showcasing its beauty and utility. Intended for a general audience of students whose degrees have no mathematics requirements, but who may be curious about practical and recreational mathematics. Not for credit in the Faculty of Science. Students who obtain UBC credit for any other mathematics course cannot in the same or later years obtain credit for MATH 230. [3-0-0]

name: Multivariable Calculus
description: Partial and directional derivatives; maxima and minima; Lagrange multipliers and second derivative test; multiple integrals and applications. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103.

name: Multivariable and Vector Calculus for Mechanical Engineering
description: Partial differentiation, extreme values, multiple integration, vector fields, line and surface integrals, the divergence and Stokes' theorems; applications to fluid mechanics: buoyancy, hydrostatic force, pipe flow, drag; applications to thermodynamics: work, entropy, heat transfer; numerical methods. Emphasis on mechanical engineering applications. [3-0-1*] Prerequisite: MATH 101 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223. Corequisite: All of MECH 222, MECH 225.

name: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Review of linear systems; nonlinear equations and applications; phase plane analysis; Laplace transforms; numerical methods. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223. Corequisite: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254.

name: Differential Equations
description: Linear ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, Fourier series and separation of variables for linear partial differential equations. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_O 200.

name: Partial Differential Equations
description: Introduction to partial differential equations; Fourier series; the heat, wave and potential equations; boundary-value problems; numerical methods. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258.

name: Differential Equations for Mechanical Engineering
description: First-order equations; linear equations; linear systems; Laplace transforms; trajectory analysis of plane nonlinear systems; translational and rotational vibrations; applications to RLC circuit analysis; numerical and graphical methods. Emphasis on mechanical engineering applications. [3-0-1*] Prerequisite: MATH 101 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223. Corequisite: All of MECH 221, MECH 224.

name: Vector Calculus for Electrical Engineering
description: Divergence, gradient, curl, theorems of Gauss and Stokes. Applications to Electrostatics and Magnetostatics. MATH_V 264 content is strongly coupled to BMEG_V 220 and ELEC_V 211 with topics and student evaluations weighted accordingly. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254. Corequisite: One of BMEG_V 220, ELEC_V 211.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Introduction to Complex Variables
description: Functions of a complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations, elementary functions, Cauchy's theorem and contour integration, Laurent series, poles and residues. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Corequisite: One of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 254, MATH 317.

name: Applied Analysis
description: Integrals involving multi-valued functions, conformal mapping and applications, analytic continuation, Laplace and Fourier transforms. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 300, MATH 305. Corequisite: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312.

name: Introduction to Probability
description: Basic notions of probability, random variables, expectation and conditional expectation, limit theorems. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254. Equivalency: STAT_V 302.

name: Introduction to Stochastic Processes
description: Discrete-time Markov chains, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains, renewal theory. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_O 203.

name: Applied Complex Analysis
description: Functions of a complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations, contour integration, Laurent series, residues, integrals of multi-valued functions, Fourier transforms. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254. Corequisite: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312.

name: Applied Linear Algebra
description: Applications of linear algebra to problems in science and engineering; use of computer algebra systems for solving problems in linear algebra. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200.

name: Euclidean Geometry
description: Classical plane geometry, solid geometry, spherical trigonometry, polyhedra, linear and affine transformations. Linear algebra proofs are used. It is suggested that MATH 307 be taken concurrently. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH 152, MATH 221 and one of MATH 220, MATH 226, CPSC 121; or (b) MATH 223.

name: Topics in Geometry
description: Topics chosen by the instructor. These may include conic sections, projective configuration, convexity, non-Euclidean geometries, fractal geometry, combinatorial problems of points in the plane. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220; or (b) MATH_V 223 or MATH_O 222.

name: Abstract Linear Algebra
description: Linear spaces, duality, linear mappings, matrices, determinant and trace, spectral theory, Euclidean structure. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 152, MATH 221 and one of MATH 220, MATH 226, CPSC 121.

name: Introduction to Number Theory
description: Euclidean algorithm, congruences, Fermat's theorem, applications. Some diophantine equations. Distribution of the prime numbers. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…Prerequisite: One of MATH 220, MATH 223, MATH 226, CPSC 121. and 9 additional credits of mathematics courses.

name: Topics in Number Theory
description: Topics chosen by the instructor. These might include: division algorithms, group theory, continued fractions, primality testing, factoring. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH_V 312.

name: Elementary Differential Equations II
description: Power series methods (ordinary and regular singular points, Bessel's equation); boundary value problems and separation of variables (Fourier series and other orthogonal series), applications to the vibrating string, heat flow, potentials. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 215, MATH_V 255, MATH_V 256, MATH_V 258, MATH_O 225.

name: Calculus IV
description: Parametrizations, inverse and implicit functions, integrals with respect to length and area; grad, div, and curl, theorems of Green, Gauss, and Stokes. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 200, MATH 226, MATH 253. One of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223 is recommended.

name: Probability with Physical Applications
description: Random variables, discrete and continuous distributions. Random walk, Markov chains, Monte Carlo methods. Characteristic functions, limit laws. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223. Corequisite: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312.

name: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: Ideas and methods of real analysis and their application. Countability and topology of the reals; convergence, continuity and differentiability of functions; metric spaces. Please consult the Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 220 or (b) a score of 55% or higher in one of MATH 223, MATH 226.

name: Real Variables I
description: The real number system; real Euclidean n-space; open, closed, compact, and connected sets; Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem; sequences and series. Continuity and uniform continuity. Differentiability and mean-value theorems. Please consult the Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH_V 226 or (b) one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254 and a score of 80% or higher in MATH_V 220.

name: Real Variables II
description: The Riemann or Riemann-Stieltjes integrals. Sequences and series of functions, uniform convergence. Approximation of continuous functions by polynomials. Fourier series. Functions from Rm to Rn , inverse and implicit function theorems. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 320.

name: Introduction to Group Theory
description: Groups, cosets, homomorphisms, group actions, p-groups, Sylow theorems, composition series, finitely generated Abelian groups. Please consult the Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 223, MATH_V 310 or (b) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and a score of 80% or higher in MATH_V 220.

name: Introduction to Rings and Modules
description: Rings, ideals, unique factorization, Euclidean rings, fields, polynomial rings, modules; structure theory of modules over a principal ideal domain. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 322.

name: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Ideas and methods of group theory and their applications. Groups, subgroups, and cosets; homomorphisms, isomorphisms, and associated theorems. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, or (b) MATH_V 223

name: Introduction to Mathematics
description: Intensive course with required tutorial. Combinatorics, probability, geometry and elementary number theory. Not for credit in the Faculty of Science. Students who obtain credit at UBC for any other mathematics course cannot in the same or later years obtain credit for MATH 335. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-2]

name: Introduction to Linear Programming
description: Linear programming problems, dual problems, the simplex algorithm, solution of primal and dual problems, sensitivity analysis. Additional topics chosen from: Karmarkar's algorithm, non-linear programming, game theory, applications. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

name: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
description: Introduction to ideas and methods of discrete mathematics and their application. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 223, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220, MATH_O 222.

name: Algebra and Coding Theory
description: Error-correcting codes via abstract and linear algebra. Emphasis on proofs and computation. Finite fields, Hamming distance and error-correction, upper and lower bounds on the size of a code, linear codes, groups and cosets, encoding and decoding schemes. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220; or (b) one of MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

name: Mathematical Game Theory
description: Introduction to mathematical game theory and its applications. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220; or (b) one of MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

name: Applied Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
description: Phase plane methods, bifurcation and stability theory, limit-cycle behavior and chaos for nonlinear differential equations with applications to the sciences. Assignments involve the use of computers. [3-1-0] Prerequisite: A score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258.

name: Engineering Analysis
description: Fourier series; auto- and cross-correlation; power spectra; discrete Fourier transform; boundary-value problems; numerical methods; partial differential equations; heat, wave, Laplace, Poisson, and wave equations. Applications to mechanical engineering and practical computing applications emphasized. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 358 or MATH 358. [3-2*-0] Prerequisite: All of MECH 224, MECH 225. Equivalency: MECH358

name: Introduction to Mathematical Modelling
description: Construction and evaluation of deterministic, stochastic, and data-driven models. Software-assisted simulations and numerical solutions involving ordinary differential equations, stochastic processes, and basic machine learning algorithms. Examples from science, engineering, and economics. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254 and one of MATH 210, CPSC 203, CPSC 210 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258.

name: Introduction to Mathematical Biology
description: Mathematical modelling of basic biological processes in ecology, physiology, neuroscience and genetics. Dynamic behavior of difference equations, differential equations, and partial differential equations, explained with reference to concrete biological examples. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of BIOL 301, MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258.

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program. Prerequisite: MATH_V 398.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

name: Applied Partial Differential Equations
description: Separation of variables, first order equations, Sturm-Liouville theory, integral transform methods. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 300, MATH 305 and one of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312.

name: Green's Functions and Variational Methods
description: Green's functions for partial differential equations. Calculus of variations. Eigenfunction expansions. Rayleigh-Ritz and finite element methods. See Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312 or (b) MATH 400.

name: Calculus of Variations
description: Classical variational problems; necessary conditions of Euler, Weierstrass, Legendre, and Jacobi; Erdmann corner conditions, transversality, convex Lagrangians, fields of extremals, sufficient conditions for optimality, numerical methods; applications to classical mechanics, engineering and economics. Recommended pre-requisites: a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 301, MATH 320, or, a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319. [3-0-0]

name: Stabilization and Optimal Control of Dynamical Systems
description: Dynamical systems; stability by Liapunov's direct method; controllability and eigenvalue assignment for autonomous linear systems; linear-quadratic regulator, time optimal control, Pontryagin maximum principle, dynamic programming; applications in engineering, economics and resource management. Recommended pre-requisites: MATH 402, and one of (a) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 301, MATH 320, or (b) a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319. [3-0-0]

name: Harmonic Analysis I
description: Harmonic analysis on Euclidean spaces, with applications to number theory, partial differential equations and geometric measure theory. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 300 and a score of 68% or higher in MATH 321. Corequisite: MATH 420.

name: Numerical Methods for Differential Equations
description: Interpolation, numerical integration, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. Practical computational methods emphasized and basic theory developed through simple models. See Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312.

name: Variational and Approximate Methods in Applied Mathematics
description: Variational and Green's function methods for ordinary and partial differential equations, introduction to finite difference, finite element and boundary element methods. See Faculty of Science Credit exclusion list:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…[3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 307, CPSC 302 and either (a) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312 or (b) MATH 400.

name: Advanced Linear Algebra
description: Topics include decompositions of linear operators, multilinear algebra, bilinear forms, metric spaces. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: A score of 68% or higher in MATH 322 and either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 320 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319.

name: Mathematical Demonstrations
description: Students will prepare material illustrating ideas and applications of mathematics and present it to audiences outside the University. Intended for third or fourth year Mathematics students and Math/Science Education students. [2-0-0; 1-0-0] or [3-0-0] Prerequisite: 24 credits in MATH.

name: Probability
description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectation, conditional probabilities, convergence of random variables, generating and characteristic functions, weak and strong laws of large numbers, central limit theorem. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 321. Prerequisite grade requirement: 68% in MATH321.

name: Stochastic Processes
description: Random walks, Markov chains, branching processes, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains, martingales, Brownian motion. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH_V 418.

name: Real Analysis I
description: Sigma-algebras, Lebesgue measure, Borel measures, measurable functions, integration, convergence theorems, Lp spaces, Holder and Minkowski inequalities, Lebesgue and/or Radon-Nikodym differentiation. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 321. Prerequisite grade requirement: 68% in MATH321.

name: Real Analysis II
description: Banach spaces, linear operators, bounded and compact operators, strong, weak, and weak* topology. Hahn-Banach, open mapping, and closed graph theorems. Hilbert spaces, symmetric and self-adjoint operators, spectral theory for bounded operators. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH_V 420.

name: Fields and Galois Theory
description: Field extensions, the Galois correspondence, finite fields, insolvability in radicals, ruler and compass constructions, additional topics chosen by instructor. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 323.

name: Commutative Algebra
description: Commutative algebra; homological algebra or representation theory of finite groups. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 323 and a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 412, MATH 422.

name: Classical Differential Geometry
description: The differential geometry of curves and surfaces in three-dimensional Euclidean space. Mean curvature and Gaussian curvature. Geodesics. Gauss's Theorema Egregium. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 223 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH 152, MATH 221; and either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 227 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH 217, MATH 254, MATH 264, MATH 317.

name: Introduction to Modern Differential Geometry
description: Smooth manifolds, smooth maps, immersions and submersions, vector fields, vector bundles, tangent and cotangent bundles, tensors and differential forms, orientation of manifolds, integration of forms, and selected topics. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 221, MATH 223 and one of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 254, MATH 264, MATH 317 and one of MATH 319, MATH 320.

name: Introduction to Topology
description: General topology, combinatorial topology, fundamental group and covering spaces, topics chosen by the instructor. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: All of MATH 321, MATH 322. Prerequisite grade requirement: 68% in MATH322,MATH321.

name: Topics in Topology
description: Homology theory, homotopy theory, manifolds, and other topics chosen by the instructor. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH_V 426.

name: Mathematical Classical Mechanics I
description: Newton's equation, conservation laws, the Euler-Lagrange equation; Hamilton's principle of least action, Hamilton's equations, Lagrangian mechanics on manifolds. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258 and one of PHYS 216, PHYS 306, ENPH 270. Corequisite: MATH 320 (waived for students with a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319).

name: Special Topics in Analysis
description: The student should consult the Mathematics Department for the particular topics offered in a given year. [3-0-0]

name: Special Topics in Algebra
description: The student should consult the Mathematics Department for the particular topics offered in a given year. [3-0-0]

name: Number Theory
description: Divisibility, congruences, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, quadratic reciprocity, advanced topics. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…. [3-0-0] Corequisite: One of MATH 320 (waived for students with a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319), MATH 322.

name: Complex Analysis
description: The residue theorem, the argument principle, conformal mapping, the maximum modulus principle, harmonic functions, representation of functions by integrals, series, and products. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 300 and either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 320 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319 and permission of the Department Head in Mathematics.

name: Mathematical Modelling: Discrete Optimization Problems
description: Formulation of real-world optimization problems using techniques such as linear programming, network flows, integer programming, dynamic programming. Solution by appropriate software. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH_V 340.

name: Graphs and Networks
description: Graph theory, emphasizing trees, tree growing algorithms, and proof techniques. Other topics chosen from shortest paths, maximum flows, minimum cost flows, matchings, and graph colouring. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: 3rd year standing and one of MATH 220, MATH 223, MATH 226 or CPSC 221.

name: Graph Theory
description: Introductory course in mostly non-algorithmic topics including: planarity and Kuratowski's theorem, graph colouring, graph minors, random graphs, cycles in graphs, Ramsey theory, extremal graph theory. Proofs emphasized. Intended for Honours students. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: A score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 220, MATH 223, MATH 226, CPSC 121. And 6 credits of MATH numbered 300 or above.

name: Mathematical Research and Writing
description: Current research topics in pure and applied mathematics are explored at the undergraduate level. Technical communication and research skills are developed. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 223, MATH_V 226, and 6 credits of MATH_V courses numbered 300 or higher.

name: Topics in the History of Mathematics I
description: Historical development of concepts and techniques in areas chosen from Geometry, Number Theory, Algebra, Calculus, Probability, Analysis. The focus is on historically significant writings of important contributors and on famous problems of Mathematics. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: 21 credits of MATH.

name: Directed Studies in Mathematics
description: Introduction to the methods of mathematical research through an exploration of a mathematical topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Written report required. Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year class standing and permission of the Department Head.

name: Honours Reading
description: Independent reading and research on a mathematical topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Intended for Honours students. Written report required. Prerequisite: Permission of the Department Head.

name: Asymptotic and Perturbation Methods
description: Asymptotic expansions. Asymptotic evaluation of integrals; WKBJ methods. Regular and singular expansions. Boundary layer theory; matched asymptotic expansions. Multiple scale techniques. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 400.

name: Projects in Mathematical Modelling
description: Computational methods for mathematical modelling. Numerical methods for partial differential equations, stochastic processes, and data-driven models. Includes student-directed projects on current research and applications. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) MATH 360 or (b) one of MATH 210, CPSC 203, CPSC 210 and one of MATH 345, MATH 361.

name: Projects in Mathematical Biology
description: Development and analysis of mathematical models for complex systems in ecology, evolution, cell biology, neurophysiology, and other biological and medical disciplines. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of MATH 361, MATH 345.

name: Advanced Dynamical Systems
description: Topics from: hyperbolic invariant sets and symbolic dynamics, global bifurcations, local bifurcations for partial differential equations, multiple bifurcations, bifurcations and symmetry, applications. Prerequisite: MATH_V 552.This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

description: Dimensional analysis, modelling, and invariance. Lie groups of transformations, infinitesimal transformations. Applications to ordinary and partial differential equations.
